expected.summary: Fourteen minutes before the anchor the third-party geocoder's EU endpoint, eu.geo.example.com, slowed down over three minutes, from a p99 of about 70 ms to about 1300 ms; the US endpoint stayed fast. shipping validates every destination address with the geocoder inside shipping.book before booking, so shipping.book for eu-west-1 requests now takes about 700 ms on average. shipping still answers 200 and logs no errors; only its address validation stats show the EU geocoder p99 far over its 300 ms budget. checkout calls shipping last in POST /checkout with a 500 ms timeout, so nearly every eu-west-1 checkout fails with 504, most through checkout's timeout on shipping and the rest through web-bff and mobile-bff timing out on checkout, while us-east-1 and us-west-2 checkouts and every other route are healthy. payment and orders run before shipping, so these customers have already been charged and have an order even though checkout reports a failure. The 504s propagate through web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. Nothing shipped and no version or config changed in our systems. The payments.example.com maintenance notice for eu-west-1 (PGW-5521), logged two minutes before onset and every five minutes since, is a red herring: payment spans in eu-west-1 stay fast and error-free and no checkout fails on payment.
contributingFactors: shipping calling the geocoder synchronously on every booking, with no budget shorter than checkout's timeout
checkout calling shipping after payment and orders, so a slow booking fails a checkout that already charged the customer
no cache or fallback for address validation when the geocoder is slow

criteria.description: Does the brief name shipping's address validation waiting on a slow third-party geocoder for eu-west-1 as the origin, with checkout's 500 ms timeout on shipping failing EU checkouts and the failures reaching edge-gateway? 5 = the geocoder, the EU segment, shipping answering 200 slowly and the victim chain. Naming checkout as the origin, or 'shipping is slow' with no cause, scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in checkout's timeouts calling shipping, shipping.book durations for eu-west-1 only, and shipping's geocoder stats showing the EU endpoint p99 rising at onset while the US endpoint stays fast? Cap at 3 unless it explains why shipping has no errors of its own.

Does it dismiss the payment provider's EU maintenance notice with evidence (payment spans fast and error-free), note that customers were charged and have orders despite the error, and avoid claiming a deploy or blaming checkout or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
